findings.title: Desktop entrypoint allow-lists can silently diverge
findings.problem: If a Desktop entrypoint value is added to _DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS (cli_analytics_handler.py:204) without updating the separately hardcoded _DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS_SQL (reader.py:629), the two lists diverge with no test catching it.
findings.impact: The served-prompt exclusion and the search exclusion would silently disagree for the new entrypoint value: a session hidden from title search could still show its auto-title in the list, or vice versa.
findings.recommendation: Derive _DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS_SQL from cli_analytics_handler._DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS (or add a test asserting the two sets stay equal).
findings.check_notes: _DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS_SQL and cli_analytics_handler._DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS now locked by test_the_sql_desktop_entrypoint_list_matches_the_handler_constant (test_reader.py:811), asserting the parsed SQL literals equal the handler frozenset.

fix.change: Added a test asserting reader._DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS_SQL's literals equal handler._DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS (no new shared module, per the plan's non-goal).

findings.title: Entrypoint whitespace/casing bypasses Desktop exclusion
findings.problem: entrypoint is stored via a bare coalesce (rollups.py:1463) with no btrim/lower normalization, unlike platform and session_title in the same VALUES list, and is compared by exact membership (_title_is_eligible) and exact SQL NOT IN (_search_arm).
findings.impact: A client sending entrypoint with stray whitespace or different casing than the three canonical literals bypasses the exclusion entirely: the Desktop auto-title is served and made searchable as if it were a real title, reproducing the exact bug this change fixes.
findings.recommendation: Normalize entrypoint (trim + lowercase) at the point it is stored or compared, matching the three canonical literals case-insensitively in both _title_is_eligible and the SQL NOT IN arm.
findings.check_notes: Comparison-side fix, not storage-side: _title_is_eligible now does strip(BLANK_CHARS).lower() (handler.py:214); _search_arm does lower(btrim(s.entrypoint, _BLANKS)) (reader.py:637). Verified by test_a_desktop_entrypoint_with_stray_case_or_whitespace_still_ignores_the_title, parametrized over mixed case, leading/trailing spaces, tab, newline.

fix.change: Compare entrypoint trimmed and lower-cased in both _title_is_eligible (cli_analytics_handler.py) and the SQL NOT IN arm (_search_arm, reader.py, via lower(btrim(s.entrypoint, _BLANKS))).

final_round.rationale: Edge-case lens found two real gaps in the new Desktop-exclusion logic, both verified live against current source: entrypoint is stored via a bare coalesce (rollups.py:1463) with no trim/lowercase, so whitespace/casing drift from the three canonical literals silently bypasses the whole exclusion in _title_is_eligible and the SQL search arm (CR-002, major); and _DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS (handler.py) / _DESKTOP_ENTRYPOINTS_SQL (reader.py) are two hand-synced literal lists with no test enforcing they stay equal (CR-001, major). Acceptance (all 8 ACs, the raw-equality decision, and all 4 non-goals) and standards (commit-format, code-quality pass; security na with no project guide but manually checked, no injection issue) both passed clean with no coverage gap, so confidence is high despite the request-changes outcome.
